messages:
maria: Heads up — seeing repeated PCIe AER resets across several GPUs in rack-a9, started ~03:15 UTC. Nodes a9-03 / a9-04 / a9-07 all showing link flap then NVML warnings. Will paste sample logs.

lee: how many cards impacted so far? serials?

maria: 6 cards across 3 hosts (a9-03, a9-04, a9-07). serials: SN-XY1234, SN-XY1235, SN-XY1236, SN-XZ2244, SN-XZ2245, SN-XZ2246. two different assembly lots but same supplier PO.

sam: this smells like the same batch that had flaky nvlink last month. any ECC count spikes or just link down?

maria: ECC counters tick up shortly after the AER messages. Not full ECC-correctable storm but noticeable.

jordan: thermal looks nominal from IPMI temps (60-68C). power rails stable. no obvious rack-level PDU blips in the window.

anna: can you drop the exact kernel logs? A stacktrace / dmesg would help.

maria: sure — snippet below (redacted):

```
[03:16:02] pcieport 0000:3f:00.0: AER: Corrected error received: id=0001
[03:16:02] pcieport 0000:3f:00.0: device [10de:1db6] error 00 on link down
[03:16:02] nvidia: GPU 0000:3f:00.0: nvml: nvmlDeviceGetMemoryErrorCounter: error 2
[03:16:04] pcieport 0000:3f:00.0: PCIe Bus Error: severity=Corrected, type=Data Link, id=00e0
[03:16:05] kernel: pci 0000:3f:00.0: slot reset completed
```

maria: full dmesg uploaded to the infra s3 bucket: s3://redwood-infra-logs/a9/1860012345/dmesg.log

ops-bot: Alert: gpu-a9-aer-reset-rate triggered — 3 events in 10m on rack a9. Auto-drain policy kickstarting.

deploy-bot: Initiated drain of a9-03 and a9-04 per policy (graceful). Jobs notified; ETA ~18m for drain completion.

lee: can we repro on a single test host? if it's firmware/BIOS maybe we can validate before RMA.

alex-vendor: thanks for the heads up — vendor support here. Please collect nvflash, BIOS, and GPU firmware versions. We will cross-check batch firmware and known PCIe PHY issues.

maria: posted versions in the bucket: nvml: 495.XX, vbios: 94.03.1, host-bios: 1.2.8. looks like two different vbios revisions, but same GPU PCB lot.

sam: proposal: 1) finish draining affected hosts 2) cold-pull one card into lab, run extended pcie stress and firmware downgrade/test 3) if repro, initiate RMA for the affected six 4) add alerting on AER per-card and throttle placement to avoid co-locating suspected cards.

jordan: agree. also suggest adding temporary kernel param pcie_aspm=off on the drained hosts when we uncordon to reduce link power transitions — low-risk mitigations while vendor investigates.

anna: note — pci=noaer would silence the errors but hide root cause; prefer to keep AER enabled and mitigate with placement + firmware.

maria: timeline: draining completes ~03:40 UTC, we'll pull one card to lab for tests by 06:00 UTC. I'll open RMA case if lab repros. I'll also schedule firmware push to a single canary node in staging.

alex-vendor: we'll prioritize checking PHY firmware and provide a test image. If we confirm manufacturing defect, we'll expedite replacements. Please share serial list (done) and logs (done).

lee: what's the capacity hit? how many GPUs offline and for how long?

maria: currently 6 GPUs offline from the drain; expected 24–36h until RMA/validation. short-term capacity loss ~2.5% of fleet in us-west. we'll shift low-priority batches out.

sam: cost note — throttling and requeues will increase batch latency; ops, flag any customer-impacting jobs? alert on queue delays over 15m.

ops-bot: Noted. Queue-delay alert threshold lowered to 15m for affected tenant groups.

jordan: postmortem action items I propose:
- add AER reset per-GPU metric and alert (3 resets / 10m)
- expand serial/lot tagging in inventory to better correlate supplier batches
- run vendor firmware audit across racks with >1 AER event
- create drain playbook for link-flap scenario (include lab test checklist)

anna: also add a canary rollout for firmware changes and require smoke test (pcie stress) before widescale.

maria: filing the incident doc now and will attach lab repro results. for now, ops will keep the affected hosts drained until we validate.

lee: thanks everyone. keep updates in this thread. :thumbsup:

maria: update 06:45 UTC — lab repro succeeded after 1.5h of pcie_stress loop; vendor asked to proceed with RMA on the six cards. opening RMA ticket now and scheduling replacements next-week delivery. :white_check_mark:

alex-vendor: RMA created #RMA-8923. We'll ship expedited units and include a test report. Will follow up directly.

sam: +1 on RCA - likely flaky PHY on a supplier sub-batch. we'll fold into next vendor review and procurement hold until replacements arrive.

maria: closing loop here — I'll post the full RCA once RMA and firmware audit complete. thanks all.
